intent.note: Task clause: 'where the case's timing is the fault, make the case's verdict independent of runner speed (inject the clock or the timeout) rather than widen a number. Show it red-first by reproducing the slow-runner timing on POSIX (inject a start-up delay).' Diff (tools/sweep-selftests.py:5253-5430, tt3c only; no product function changed): the hanging block now leaves a witness file after its print (tt_hang, tt_witness), tt3c runs the suite at deadlines 1,2,4,8 and stops at the first run whose witness exists, and the first row (deadline 1, print delayed 2.0s) injects a slow start-up so a run that printed nothing is judged on every runner. Every run must still show ok False, 'FAIL x-block DID NOT REPORT ... did not finish within Ns', 'FAIL y-block DID NOT REPORT ... not started: the sweep's deadline of <that run's deadline>s had passed', no 'PASS ty1', output ending 'SELFTEST FAILED: 0/2 cases passed', and took < 30s; the witnessed run must carry the partial line exactly once, an unwitnessed one at most once; the case fails if no run is witnessed (tt_tries[-1]['printed']). Not weakened: a product that stopped replaying a deadline-cut staged suite or stopped naming the killed or the refused block fails the x/y regexes and the 0/2 tail on EVERY run, including the injected-delay one; a product that dropped or duplicated the partial fails the witnessed run's partial == 1. The witness is written after the print and flushed, so witness-present with partial == 0 is a genuine product failure, not a race. The adaptive ladder is a residual dependence on speed only in the sense that a runner needing more than 8s to reach the print fails the case with every deadline tried named in the label; the verdict is not otherwise a function of speed. The executor's diagnosis (product right, case timing the fault) is consistent with the diff and with the CI observation (only the one windows leg failed, with the replay, x and y all correct and only the partial line absent). Claim vs diff: the outcome describes the diff accurately (fixture text and tt3c body only; dependants unaffected except the suite's own seconds, about 1s more, in .github/sweep-costs.json, which is not re-recorded). The pre-existing tt3b assertion tt_files['split-quick'].count('time.sleep') == 0 still holds for the new tt_split template. The brief-mismatch remark in the outcome is an orchestrator note, not a diff matter. I did not re-run the selftest (the recorded gate run is passed).
